analysis.title: Skyworks Solutions Inc. (SWKS): Benefits of diversification and scale likely to be offset by smartphones headwinds, Reinstate at Sell
key_insights: GS reinstates SWKS at Sell with a 12-month price target of $78 against a $85.40 price (8.7% downside). The target is 12X P/E on normalized earnings of $6.50, 1X below the stock's 5-year median NTM P/E.
The Skyworks-Qorvo merger closed October 5, 2026. GS updates its model to reflect it and models FY27/28/29 revenue of $7.4bn/$7.8bn/$8.2bn, up from $3.9bn/$4.5bn for FY27/FY28 in the old model.

Qorvo gives the combined company about 40% exposure to defense/aerospace, automotive and industrial markets. GS expects Broad Markets to reach 45% of revenue by FY29, while smartphones stay about 60% of sales through FY28E.

GS expects smartphone exposure to hold SWKS growth below peers. It forecasts pro forma revenue growth of about 8% in CY27, versus much faster growth at most other analog and digital semiconductor names.

Smartphone demand is weak, especially in Android, as higher DRAM prices and component costs have pushed OEM price increases. GS models smartphone units down 10% YoY in 2026 and up 2% in each of 2027 and 2028, and expects DRAM prices to stay elevated through 2027/28.
A Nikkei report cited by GS says Apple has told suppliers of order reductions for its latest iPhone models. GS still views Apple as better positioned than Android OEMs.

Combining the two smartphone RF businesses should reduce competitive intensity and pricing pressure, and should lower cycle-to-cycle earnings volatility. Scale should also support higher R&D spend and more disciplined pricing.
GS models company-guided cost synergies of $500mn annualized within 24-36 months of close. It assumes $140mn of COGS synergies by FY29 and $150mn of OpEx synergies in FY27, rising to $340mn by FY28.

Modeled synergy margin uplift is 170 bps at gross margin. The text says 360 bps at operating margin, while the Exhibit 4 title says 420 bps. Non-GAAP gross margin (excl. SBC) is modeled at 48.5%/50.6%/52.9% and operating margin at 24.0%/28.0%/30.1% for FY27/28/29.
GS non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) estimates for FY27/28/29 are $6.05/$7.60/$8.80. They are 0%/3%/10% below Visible Alpha consensus and above GS's old $5.10/$7.25 for FY27/FY28.

On relative value, GS sees a narrow discount for SWKS (about 12.7x CY27 P/E, a 20% discount to the analog peer median of 15.9x) against a 5-year median discount of 40%. It sees better risk/reward elsewhere in analog, where aerospace/defense, industrial, datacenter and even automotive are recovering.

SWKS has historically traded at a ~47% median discount to the SOX. The SOX trades at ~17X versus SWKS at ~13X GS NTM EPS, so the discount is narrower than usual, which GS reads as limited relative upside. Apple could be up to ~50% of estimated sales.
FY4Q26 results were in line with the Street: revenue $1.05bn vs $1.04bn, gross margin 44.4% vs 44.5%, non-GAAP EPS $1.28 vs $1.27.
FY1Q27 guidance is well below the Street: revenue midpoint $1.85bn vs $1.99bn, and non-GAAP EPS $1.25 vs $1.64, which is 24% below.
Company synergy guidance: $150mn of OpEx synergies within FY27 (weighted to 2H), an exit run rate of $250-$300mn annualized, and $500mn within 24-36 months after close.

GS would turn more constructive on evidence of a smartphone bottoming or return to growth, faster growth in aerospace/defense, datacenter or industrial, faster synergy capture, or better pricing power at Skyworks' largest smartphone customers. A broader re-rating of peer valuations would also help.

market_movers.rationale: Qorvo diversification and synergies are offset by roughly 60% smartphone exposure and limited visibility on a recovery. The valuation discount to analog peers has narrowed versus history.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees better risk/reward in analog peers with cyclical upturns in industrial, aerospace/defense and datacenter. SWKS growth is held back by smartphone exposure.
Unit shipments are modeled down 10% YoY in 2026 on higher DRAM and component costs. Recovery is modeled at only 2% in 2027 and 2028, with low visibility.

earnings_insights: FY4Q26 (reported, non-GAAP excl. SBC): revenue $1,046mn vs Street $1,036mn (+1.0%), up 11.9% QoQ and down 4.9% YoY. Gross margin 44.4% vs Street 44.5%. EPS $1.28 vs Street $1.27.
FY1Q27 guidance (company, non-GAAP excl. SBC): revenue $1.80-1.90bn, midpoint $1.85bn vs Street $1.985bn (-6.8%). EPS midpoint $1.25 vs Street $1.64 (-24.0%).
GS FY27E/FY28E/FY29E non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) estimates are $6.05/$7.60/$8.80, versus old $5.10/$7.25 for FY27/FY28. They are 0%/3%/10% below Visible Alpha consensus.
GS GAAP-basis diluted EPS (pre-exceptionals) estimates are $4.49/$5.98/$7.09 for FY27E/28E/29E, against $3.60 for FY26.
GS FY27E revenue is $7,431mn, 89% above the old $3,923mn, reflecting the Qorvo merger closed October 5, 2026. Revenue growth is 87.7% in FY27E, then 5.1% and 4.6% in FY28E and FY29E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects industry units to fall in 2026 and recover only modestly, which limits near-term earnings power for smartphone-exposed RF suppliers.

macro_indicators.reading: Materially spiked in 2026, expected to stay elevated in 2027/28
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher memory costs push up OEM phone prices, which weighs on consumer demand, especially for Android devices.

trade_ideas.description: Sell SWKS, 12-month price target $78 (about 8.7% downside from $85.40)
trade_ideas.rationale: Smartphone exposure of about 60% dampens growth and the valuation discount to analog peers has narrowed versus history.
trade_ideas.risk: Faster smartphone recovery, faster growth in adjacent broad markets, or better-than-expected synergy capture.

risk_factors: Stronger-than-expected smartphone recovery could lift both fundamentals and the multiple (upside risk to the Sell call).
Faster-than-expected growth in aerospace & defense, automotive or datacenter could beat GS estimates.
Better-than-expected synergy capture could lift margin forecasts.
Customer concentration, with Apple up to ~50% of estimated sales, and further risk of negative smartphone revisions.
Elevated DRAM prices and reported Apple iPhone order cuts could weigh on smartphone demand.

tension_points.bull_case: The merger adds about 40% exposure to defense/aerospace, automotive and industrial markets and about $500mn of cost synergies. Consolidating two large RF suppliers could ease pricing pressure and reduce earnings volatility.
tension_points.bear_case: Smartphones remain about 60% of revenue through FY28E. Smartphone units are modeled down 10% in 2026, Apple is up to ~50% of sales, and FY1Q27 guidance came in well below the Street.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of a smartphone market bottoming or return to growth, or a broader re-rating of peer valuations, would make GS more constructive.

theme_stances.key_argument: Visibility into the timing and magnitude of a smartphone recovery is low, making it a near-term drag on Skyworks' earnings profile.
theme_stances.evidence: visibility into both the timing and magnitude of this recovery in smartphones remains quite low

theme_stances.key_argument: Scale, diversification and cost synergies should improve margins and earnings power, but not enough to offset smartphone headwinds.
SWKS offers less attractive risk/reward than analog peers with faster growth and clearer cyclical recovery.
